takeaway: IMN keeps Pacífico Norte partly cloudy with only a chance of peninsula rain this afternoon, while heat stays near 36°C at Nicoya; tropical waves OT#44 (overnight) and OT#45 (Sunday) plus ITCZ moisture are the weekend–early-week shower drivers. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development interest remains well offshore southwest of Mexico or farther west, not aimed at Nicoya.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun)
periods.pattern: Today: IMN Pacífico Norte — partly cloudy morning/afternoon with possibility of peninsula rain; general ITCZ instability favors stronger Pac Central/Sur storms more than Guanacaste. Sat–Sun: IMN weekly flags OT#45 Sunday activating the ITCZ, with Pac Norte rains/aguaceros more significant Sunday into early next week. GFS 06Z and ECMWF 00Z 24-h precip maps keep Nicoya mostly light (~0.05–0.5 in / 24 h) through Sun — no locked heavy pulse. Papagayo still fresh today (NHC).
periods.implications: Mornings still the better outdoor window; finish plans before afternoon convection, especially Sunday if OT#45 verifies. Heat remains a limiter (IMN Nicoya max ~36.2°C).
periods.confidence: High for no nearby TC and typical wet-season cells. Moderate on Sunday amounts (IMN wetter language vs light model maps).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu)
periods.pattern: IMN weekly expects Pac Norte rains into early next week after OT#45. Deterministic GFS/ECMWF keep light–moderate Nicoya totals rather than a multi-day temporal. GFS and GEFS mean 850 hPa / MSLP around Tue–Wed 23 Sep show light Caribbean easterlies and only weak Pacific-side flow — no closed Central American gyre in the means.
periods.implications: Treat early-week rain as on-and-off afternoon cells, not a guaranteed temporales. Keep late-day plans flexible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances; low–moderate for sustained Pacific-side temporales or gyre.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain. CPC GTH (valid 23 Sep–6 Oct, text updated 15 Sep) still favors below-average Caribbean rainfall weeks 2–3; EPAC genesis risk is coastal Mexico / open EPAC, not CR.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Still loosely around mid–late next week (~Tue–Wed 22–23 Sep) only if flanking lows and sustained Pacific SW low-level flow develop; not supported as a closed gyre in current ensemble means
gyreWatch.supporting: IMN weekly OT#45 / ITCZ language into early next week; GFS deterministic can still show weaker pressure and more variable Pacific-side 850 flow at longer range on some frames.
gyreWatch.conflicting: GEFS mean 06Z and AIFS-ENS 00Z ~f120 (Wed 23) lack a closed Central American gyre and keep light easterlies over the western Caribbean; GFS 06Z f144 similarly lacks a nearby closed low over CR/Nicaragua; NHC has no disturbance near CR; IMN sub-seasonal still Pacific deficit. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities.

whatChanged: Yesterday’s explicit IMN Nicoya afternoon-storm call softens today to “possibility of rain on the peninsula,” while the weekly outlook still points to a wetter Pac Norte Sunday–early next week via OT#45. Model maps no longer highlight yesterday’s ECMWF-wetter Sat or GFS Sun pulse — GFS 06Z and ECMWF 00Z stay light–moderate over Nicoya. The late-week gyre idea remains watch-only and is still not ensemble-backed (GEFS/AIFS-ENS).
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Fri–Sun before convective peaks; Sunday is the day to watch more closely if OT#45 activates. Worth planning around: heat (IMN Nicoya max ~36.2°C), possible afternoon showers, and Papagayo E 15–20 kt with seas ~6–8 ft today easing Sat onward to lighter NW–N winds (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113).
